notes.title: Red Haze's final update will hit in December
notes.notes:
Red Haze's long awaited final content update will be releasing in December of 2025. This is the final content update, everything in the game will be fully playable. The only other updates afterward will just be to fix any bugs that might creep up for anything found afterward.



The update will add the top of the lighthouse to the game, Ending A will become available, and the A-Z Door will open up for anyone who's collected all 26 regular endings (the two bonus Halloween & Out of Bounds endings aren't needed, but they unlock other things). It'll probably hit in the first half of December, but don't want to narrow it to a specific date until I'm 100% certain, just wanted to give a heads up when its coming broadly ahead of time. I want to keep most of what this update entails a surprise, but I hope y'all will look forward to it!



Additionally, the DLC piece for Red Haze, "Bruises Glimmer in Starlight," will also be receiving a major update at the same time as the main game. There will be updates to the story of Gretta and the gameplay from the original DLC, but also her story will become "Chapter 1". A new free content expansion updated will be added to the DLC, "Chapter 2", telling a brand new story with a new protagonist and new gameplay scenario that's directly tied to the story of Red Haze. The price for the DLC won't increase or anything, just be free new content for owners of the DLC that hits on the same day as the final update to the main game.

[dynamiclink href="https://store.steampowered.com/app/1553270/Red_Haze__Bruises_Glimmer_in_Starlight/"][/dynamiclink]

Again, I hope y'all look forward to it!



For other Yai Gameworks going-ons, I'll be releasing the final update to Feast Your Eyes on August 31st (the 10-year anniversary of the Steam release of the original Close Your Eyes), a direct story sequel to the original Close Your Eyes. This update will have a major art overhaul to Chapters 1 & 2 of that game, add voice acting, add new areas, new story, new horrors, as well as Steam achievements. And finally, it'll release Chapter 3, finishing that game's story and making that game complete as well.

[dynamiclink href="https://store.steampowered.com/app/712260/Feast_Your_Eyes/"][/dynamiclink]

Finally, on October 14th/15th, I'll be releasing a brand new game titled Inferbito. Far more on that in September/October. I hope it'll interest you.

[dynamiclink href="https://store.steampowered.com/app/1624490/Inferbito/"][/dynamiclink]

I hope you guys are having a wonderful day!

notes.title: Red Haze Big July 11th Update OUT NOW!
notes.notes:
Alright! Here's the promised update from the last update. This update includes:


Endings B, D & X added to the game.
Two new monsters with two new death scenes.
25+ new rooms added to the game.
227 new voice lines, including previous endings and quips where Rockette wasn't voiced she now is.
3 new non-ending cutscenes and 2 new "Story Quests" (which make permanent progress points).
Few new secrets.
Think I've fixed every bug reported to me, though sure new ones will creep up I need to fix.


This completes the "Main Area" of Red Haze! The game is almost finished, just one more update to go to add Ending A and the A-Z Door into the game (and get Starry voiced in Ending Q in the last recording session with Danuta). I wouldn't hold off playing the game just for the next update though, as Ending A and the A-Z Door both are pretty strong "points of no return", separated really from the rest of the game. If you do the "story quest" to unlock the pathway to Ending A right now, it's blockaded for now but will remain unlocked for the next update.

I hope y'all are having a wonderful day, I'm releasing this on my birthday actually. And I hope you enjoy the new content in Red Haze!

notes.title: July 11th (12th in some regions) Red Haze update detailed

2 new monsters (along with two new death scenes)

27 new rooms

The final update will hopefully land in August, and include the following:
-Ending A
-The A-Z Door finally openable
-Ending Q will finally have Starry be voiced

And then Red Haze will be finished!

If thinking of holding off playing until the final update, I actually would say there's no real good reason to wait. Ending A & the A-Z Door both have very "point of no return" elements and content to them that make them a bit separated from the rest of the game. With this update, all of the "main area" of Red Haze is concluded and fully explorable. You can even do the "story quest" to access Ending A right now, but it'll be blockaded until the final update (but stay unlocked for anyone to easily access if they do so now before the final update).

Anyways, I'm excited for this upcoming Red Haze update and to very soon finally mark Red Haze as completed. I really hope you enjoy the final batch of Red Haze content! Have a wonderful day!

notes.title: Lag Fixes, April Fools Joke Version Over, and Some Notes
notes.notes:
Okay! So I've done something that will hopefully fix all the lag issues in Red Haze. Should see all around a GREAT performance boost in the game. I won't promise it's 100% fixed, but all rooms should be performing quite a bit better with most people, and there should be zero lag for those with half-way decent computers. This took longer than I hoped since the fix was kind of a dumb thing with the game's files that risked corrupting save files, so I had been troubleshooting how to do this without corrupting save files and I think I've done it! I did put a one-time save file message that'll pop up once about moving save files if you don't have your save file, but I think most everyone should have their save files still accessible.

The one downside to this method is for some users who've played other games that use nw.js, you may get a message about how it can't access your profile. This occurs as nw.js detects this is an older version of nw.js, but I need to use an older version currently until Greenworks updates to allow people to take Steam Screenshots, but hopefully will be fixed in the next few months (I need to wait for Greenworks to update, and hope it does before the Big Update is finally done).

Now this also I think may inadvertently fix the issue of people crashing with the "Chess" Dummy enemy and Big Picture Mode overlay issues, but I cannot confirm this and it's more hoping on my part due to the changes made.

Outside of that, April Fools Joke Edition of Red Haze is now over, the game is back to normal. However, a few updates including some bug fixes, a few new rooms and areas, and a few new secrets are still included without the joke elements.

Hope to keep Red Haze update love rolling very soon, but won't promise any dates yet since I'm sure many of you have noticed I've been multi-tasking a lot of projects. But I want to finish Red Haze's chapter soon, so here's hoping.

notes.title: Yai Gameworks upcoming game release plans and news
notes.notes:
I thank you all who participated in the Yai Gameworks 2018 Questionnaire survey a couple months back. As many are probably aware of I am a man of many ideas, and indeed probably too many. I release 2-3 games a year but dates get pushed back, some are left idling for months to years before they eventually release. I won’t promise this won’t change, but as a solid effort applying some strategies I’ve learned within the last few months and a plight to achieve one of my dream games, Complete Isolation, I will explain a crazy thing I’m about to try and apply myself to do, then the reasoning, and finally the specifics.

Between February of 2018 to April of 2019 I want to release 12 video games onto Steam.

Now there’s a few reasons I have chosen to attempt this honestly foolish errand, especially foolish for me. I originally had set my sights to work on a dream project I’ve had in my head for many years, my first actual big project titled, “Complete Isolation.” I held a funding campaign for this game back in 2013 on Indiegogo, who’s funding has been used for all my projects to produce the music you all hear in my games. Still, here we are five years later and CI still does not exist. I want to make it, I desperately do, and I originally had planned to commit myself to it this year. That was until all my analysis, self-reflection, crunching, talking with others, and reason pointed me to pursuing another goal first, to do something else foolish first so that CI would be a less foolish endeavor and a safer bet.

You see, Complete Isolation is planned as an episodic gameplay experience. Episodic releases work best on a timed release manner; being timely with episodes is important. That means having a good groundwork you can easily build off of, self-discipline, a solid plan and commitment, and short development cycles. These are all things I need to master, and trying to wrangle that first-hand on an episodic game would be setting many up for disappointment of delays when I inevitability failed to deliver on time. I need to practice this first, but in a form that isn’t both as anti-consumer and as financially risky as a longer term episodic game. Climb a hill before a mountain kinda’ thing.

Add to this CI needs to look the part, it has a bigger investment, bigger cost, and as I’d be tackling a large chunk of the game myself from coding to design to music and writing and voice directing  I’d need someone to do the art, a pretty sizable amount of drawn art and sprite work as well. But the needed art amount is hefty, and I’m not in a financial position to offer a decent payment upfront. Rincs, my partner in crime on projects who’s done the drawn art on my projects, hasn’t seen a cent from Yai Gameworks sales and I feel awful about it. I need her for a longer term but don’t want to run her ragged, and need to pay her properly for her work. I should save up and split profits, but even that is a huge uncertainty. I need to secure more income, and allow her more time to do art for the project between her busy life.

Add to all of this having Yai Gameworks name out there and more experience under our belt can only be a good thing.

I decided to propose a challenge to myself, a series of experimental games on a planned and tight schedule. This is a way to work myself to a position where I can hopefully form the experience and conviction needed to do an episodic structure, all while getting more games and experiences under my belt. All while hopefully earning some money and making some more things available to all of you guys I hope that y’all enjoy. It may even work out to be a good way to market it as the steps up to try and achieve Complete Isolation.

There’s more to all of this. But I plan to in the upcoming week make a video detailing it all a little further. This plan isn’t just to make more games however, it’s to make an over-a-year plan and stick to it. The first game of this challenge is already released, it can be found as Please Love My Computer Game on Steam. However, I will now detail the rest of the plan to you all. I cannot guarantee I will be able to meet and achieve what I hope to, but I can tell you I’m going to be working hard to achieve my own dreams which I view this as a crucial step towards.

So if things pan out, what can you all expect?

APRIL 2018:
-”The Crack I Found That Taketh”
A nearly dialogue-less 3D exploration and discovery experimental game about a crack in the floor.

MAY 2018:
-”Red Haze” big content update
The big content update for Red Haze hits, including all endings, new areas, new story, new secrets, lag fixes, more scene skips, and more.

JUNE 2018:
-”Unlabeled”
An 8-bit game inspired by Hellnight and Nanashi no Game about an NPC in a small RPG village that one day gains sentience, and begins to be stalked by an ever-evolving monstrosity. Partner up with other people in the village that can permanently die at anytime, leading you down different storyline paths.

JULY 2018
-”Hellscape”
You are a Demigod on a dying world abandoned by the True Gods. Walk among men and explore the hellscape left behind,meeting devotees, non-believers, deformed and withering beings who may love or hate you. You may guide them to nurish a future, or trample them into oblivion. What gift may you give a disgusting world with no hope?

AUGUST 2018
-”The Killing Kink Nunster”
A B-Horror Comedy game about a group of college kids who all are a bit messed up and kinky getting trapped in a cathedral with the monstrous nun known as the Killing Kink Nunster, who wishes to eradicate their sin and pay their dues with their blood. It’s a lot weirder and even more twisted than you think.
-”Close Your Eyes -Anniversary Remake”
A remake of Close Your Eyes with new content, a new scenario, a remake of Girl’s Graveyard, new modes, a new open world connecting world, and a lot of surprises to prep for the eventual sequel.

SEPTEMBER 2018:
-”Cootie Patootie”
A reimagining of a previous game I made for Ludum Dare. Join Cootie Patrootie as she goes on a magical journey of self-discovery to find love!

OCTOBER 2018
-”RODE: Remorse Observation Dream Emulation”
For the 20th anniversary of the cult gem, LSD: Dream Emulator, have this 3D first-person love letter to it.

NOVEMBER 2018:
-”Box Pusher”
A nice relaxing little puzzle game about pushing boxes. It might seem a little off, but that’s probably nothing.

JANUARY 2019:
-”The Seafaring Incident”
You’re on a seven day cruise in the Pacific, but something is very wrong. Over the course of 7 days you’ll need to investigate these mysterious circumstances  and work out how to keep your head above water.

FEBRUARY 2019:
-”The Silhouette of the Alluring Rose”
A more normalized RPG Maker-esque dark fantasy puzzle horror starring a frilly girl… IN 3D!

April 2019:
-”(untitled at this time)”
An experimental little MMO experience in a Yume Nikki-esque exploration game.

Regardless, this will be a busy year, and I hope to surprise you all throughout the year. The easiest way to keep up with Yai Gameworks news, socialize, little surprises, and collaborate is to join the official Yai Gameworks discord, which you may find here: https://discord.gg/EVwaARY

These are all things I need to master, and trying to wrangle that first-hand on an episodic game would be setting many up for disappointment of delays when I inevitability failed to deliver on time. I need to practice this first, but in a form that isn’t both as anti-consumer and as financially risky as a longer term episodic game. Climb a hill before a mountain kinda’ thing.

Add to this CI needs to look the part, it has a bigger investment, bigger cost, and as I’d be tackling a large chunk of the game myself from coding to design to music and writing and voice directing  I’d need someone to do the art, a pretty sizable amount of drawn art and sprite work as well. But the needed art amount is hefty, and I’m not in a financial position to offer a decent payment upfront. Rincs, my partner in crime on projects who’s done the drawn art on my projects, hasn’t seen a cent from Yai Gameworks sales and I feel awful about it. I need her for a longer term but don’t want to run her ragged, and need to pay her properly for her work. I should save up and split profits, but even that is a huge uncertainty. I need to secure more income, and allow her more time to do art for the project between her busy life.

Add to all of this having Yai Gameworks name out there and more experience under our belt can only be a good thing.

I decided to propose a challenge to myself, a series of experimental games on a planned and tight schedule. This is a way to work myself to a position where I can hopefully form the experience and conviction needed to do an episodic structure, all while getting more games and experiences under my belt. All while hopefully earning some money and making some more things available to all of you guys I hope that y’all enjoy. It may even work out to be a good way to market it as the steps up to try and achieve Complete Isolation.

There’s more to all of this. But I plan to in the upcoming week make a video detailing it all a little further. This plan isn’t just to make more games however, it’s to make an over-a-year plan and stick to it. The first game of this challenge is already released, it can be found as Please Love My Computer Game on Steam. However, I will now detail the rest of the plan to you all. I cannot guarantee I will be able to meet and achieve what I hope to, but I can tell you I’m going to be working hard to achieve my own dreams which I view this as a crucial step towards.

APRIL 2018:
-”The Crack I Found That Taketh”
A nearly dialogue-less 3D exploration and discovery experimental game about a crack in the floor.

MAY 2018:
-”Red Haze” big content update
The big content update for Red Haze hits, including all endings, new areas, new story, new secrets, lag fixes, more scene skips, and more.

JUNE 2018:
-”Unlabeled”
An 8-bit game inspired by Hellnight and Nanashi no Game about an NPC in a small RPG village that one day gains sentience, and begins to be stalked by an ever-evolving monstrosity. Partner up with other people in the village that can permanently die at anytime, leading you down different storyline paths.

JULY 2018
-”Hellscape”
You are a Demigod on a dying world abandoned by the True Gods. Walk among men and explore the hellscape left behind,meeting devotees, non-believers, deformed and withering beings who may love or hate you. You may guide them to nurish a future, or trample them into oblivion. What gift may you give a disgusting world with no hope?

AUGUST 2018
-”The Killing Kink Nunster”
A B-Horror Comedy game about a group of college kids who all are a bit messed up and kinky getting trapped in a cathedral with the monstrous nun known as the Killing Kink Nunster, who wishes to eradicate their sin and pay their dues with their blood. It’s a lot weirder and even more twisted than you think.
-”Close Your Eyes -Anniversary Remake”
A remake of Close Your Eyes with new content, a new scenario, a remake of Girl’s Graveyard, new modes, a new open world connecting world, and a lot of surprises to prep for the eventual sequel.

SEPTEMBER 2018:
-”Cootie Patootie”
A reimagining of a previous game I made for Ludum Dare. Join Cootie Patrootie as she goes on a magical journey of self-discovery to find love!

OCTOBER 2018
-”RODE: Remorse Observation Dream Emulation”
For the 20th anniversary of the cult gem, LSD: Dream Emulator, have this 3D first-person love letter to it.

NOVEMBER 2018:
-”Box Pusher”
A nice relaxing little puzzle game about pushing boxes. It might seem a little off, but that’s probably nothing.

JANUARY 2019:
-”The Seafaring Incident”
You’re on a seven day cruise in the Pacific, but something is very wrong. Over the course of 7 days you’ll need to investigate these mysterious circumstances  and work out how to keep your head above water.

FEBRUARY 2019:
-”The Silhouette of the Alluring Rose”
A more normalized RPG Maker-esque dark fantasy puzzle horror starring a frilly girl… IN 3D!

April 2019:
-”(untitled at this time)”
An experimental little MMO experience in a Yume Nikki-esque exploration game.

Regardless, this will be a busy year, and I hope to surprise you all throughout the year. The easiest way to keep up with Yai Gameworks news, socialize, little surprises, and collaborate is to join the official Yai Gameworks discord, which you may find here: https://discord.gg/EVwaARY

notes.title: Big Update-Update, and Pricing News
notes.notes:
Been busy working on the Red Haze update and one other project, so I thought I should give an update on both as Halloween has passed.

The update is delayed a little bit, I was debating whether to release it in chunks or all at once. I've redesigned a lot of the eventing to help with the lag issue, fixed a few bugs and typos I know about, and am finished with adding new secrets in previous rooms. I could release that right now, but I've decided to hold off a bit as I want to do an 'all at once' release I think. And as I've been working, I've been expanding some of my ideas and the updates gotten a little bigger. The original plans I had for the Lighthouse are done, but I added a few more rooms and a new far more dramatic finale for the Lighthouse path I hope you'll all enjoy, but isn't quite done yet. There's also a new area which kind of increased in scale, and as I've been increasing the areas and the story a bit I also realized I need to get back into contact with Serene Harper, the voice actress of Rockette, for some new lines (as it'd be weird if some of these scenes weren't voiced when so much of the game already is).

As the game's scope has increased, and I'm starting to realize Red Haze without exaggeration is going to be a 15-30 hour long game if you're going for all the endings/secrets and such, I have decided I'm going to increase the game's price at the end of the year from $1.99 USD to $2.99 USD. I thought I should announce this ahead of time, and the change will not happen until early next year after the Autumn and Winter Steam Sales. Red Haze will be available during both sales for $1.75 USD (12% off), but after those sales the overall base price will go up to $2.99 USD partially to reflect the boost of content within the game. I hope the game will be worth it.

I'm learning I should stop putting dates on things, what usually happens is I have a bad tendency to both get distracted/caught up with life things, and then while I'm being very productive I start getting ideas and being the type of person I am I decide to implement those ideas as well rather than just sticking with what I originally had planned in scope. I think accepting and dealing with this part of myself is crucial, and at least having done several games in the last couple years I'm becoming more aware of how I work. I have a bad tendency to delay things if I date them, so I might just take the stance it will be done when it's done, and even still I end up releasing a few games every year. This will not change next year either, I have several projects in partial completion stages that will probably see the light of day next year, and for this year my goal is to finish the Red Haze update and release one more project of mine before the year is up. To decide which one I'll be asking the official Yai Gameworks Discord, which if you're interested to join that you can find a pinned topic for it in the Close Your Eyes: Intermission Steam Discussion Board.

Depending how strong work ends up being, how I balance it with my other project decided to finish this year, and how much I decide to expand and get done, the Red Haze Update could be finished anywhere from this week to early December. The truth is if I focused solely on it and kept to my original plan it could be done as early as tomorrow, but I want to expand it and I think it'll be a better update that will hopefully blow fans of the game away if I put in the extra work and content. I do thank you guys for sticking with me even if I'm absolutely terrible at dating things and getting things done on the time I say I will get them done, I'm going to try to improve on promising dates in the future because I've realized I'm terrible at it.

If you have any questions, feel free to ask in this comments updates and I'll try to answer while I'm focused on this update for the next week or a few (whichever it ends up being). Thank you for you time, and hope you all had a happy Halloween!

notes.notes:
Hey, so letting you all know firstly Red Haze development isn't dead. What I've been doing is with Steam Direct on the horizon I've been working myself rigid to get several projects to a presentable enough state to post them all on Steam Greenlight on April 28th. Thanks for your time and patience on these two big updates, and know I'll be posting like, 3-7 projects on Greenlight on the 28th, most won't release super soon but want to get them through Greenlight now while I have the chance.

notes.title: Red Haze Patch 1.2 Notes
notes.notes:
UPDATE: 1.2 is all live now.

So there will basically be multiple updates and then a bigger update every day it seems. Some people have been posting thoughts on the discussion board which has given me a lot of ideas of how to improve the overall experience. There's a lot I'm starting to put together that should roll out in the next few days I'll explain after this post. Make sure to post thoughts, requests, suggestions, critiques, questions, opinions, whatever on the discussion board. Hearing back from others is incredibly helpful for me.

And of course if you spot any bugs or typos, report them here: http://steamcommunity.com/app/428860/discussions/0/135508833655990580/

Now unfortunately I didn't get done with the Trafficking Dungeon yet, I am keeping it in its unfinished state for the moment so you can't trigger things you shouldn't yet that would make people miss out on stuff. I got caught up fixing up some other aspects and watching Let's Plays of Red Haze honestly. If things go well that should be tomorrow though. But I did a few things for this update.


---


RED HAZE 1.2 NOTES: 

-Fixed a lot of bugs, typos, and minor things. Watching Let's Plays paid off since I saw things some people didn't realize were bugs I've fixed. And continue with the wonderful reports from you guys, I'm squashing what bugs are found as much as I can. Also fixed up a few typos that went under the radar unnoticed by most.

-Tone down the difficulty of a few enemies. So some spoilers, but specifically the [spoiler]Custodian in the Southeast Hall is now a tad easier. Just a tad, most people probably won't spot the difference but he was a bit of a doozy before due to one aspect I've toned down now.[/spoiler] The biggest change though is in another enemy type. [spoiler]The Mannequin enemy, or as I call it the Mannenmy, has been toned down in difficulty tremendously. A lot of people were wasting their adrenaline on the gruesome beast so I made their behavoir just a bit dumber so they're easier to pass... But not too easy.[/spoiler]

-Added more Adrenaline spots to the game. 

-One of the scenes in the Trafficking Dungeon is now fully voiced, but I recommend not delving there until the update tomorrow.

-There's four achievements you can get as well, two of which are accessible right now. This is also the final achievement list, I won't be adding anymore.


---


There's also a lot of early hooks for a few ideas. So thanks to some wonderful feedback, here's some things I'm planning to add in the next few days: 

PLANS FOR UPCOMING PATCHES:

-Trafficking Dungeon Completed... obviously.

-Implementation to be able to skip the prologue bit after a few runs if you do something in the game, though it may effect some things.

-Some sort of thing at the start of the game you can interact with to turn some special settings on and off. Specifically, some computers (not many but some) have issues with the rooms with Fog in it, the opacity effects don't work so the rooms are unseeable, so adding an option to turn fog on/off. Also going to add an option to turn the 3D in 3D sections on/off, but know they 100% are designed with 3D in mind but want to give the option. I also will add an ability for captions for the voice you sometimes here, might break some immersion but be able to understand what it's saying at least.

-New hidden scenes/effects/ending effects. Want to add additional things that can happen by chance to the game. Some triggered only to be possible once you've done other things. But if don't worry, if you've already been playing the game this will in no way lock you out to these events, in fact you're more likely to have already triggered the conditions for some things I'll be adding, so be able to experience them sooner than later when released if things fall into place for each one... Sorry for being cryptic with that, but don't want to give too much away!


---


I hope those getting lost in the Haze are having a good time, tomorrow update should be a big one if I get as much done as I hope to. Just keep the feedback and discussion coming! I'm hoping to continue shaping Red Haze into something progressively better, and will be at this for the next few weeks. Because of all the other stuff I'm adding, there might be a light delay to the Lighthouse Upper Floors and Final Door as have been focused on adding other features, but don't worry, I am working on them too!

Happy trails to all of those wandering the haze~

notes.notes:
Okay, so some of you who've had the game for a bit may have noticed it updated several times yesterday. I also just released another update. These updates will be pretty regular over the next few weeks.

I've been taking early feedback and making some changes to the game. Before I post the details of the updates, please if you have any thoughts/requests/issues, post them in the Discussion Boards. I am in fact listening and making changes to the game based on feedback. I of course won't do every request, but requesting things helps me think over it and decide if I think it's a good idea or not.

Anyways, because of some requests and such, here's some things that have been patched in since release yesterday: 


-Made it so after you've seen four unique endings, the credits will go 2.5x faster in every ending hereafter. Also if you get an ending you've already gotten before, credits will go 3x faster automatically.

-New mechanic: If you get caught and thrown into the Well by the Custodian three times, on the fourth time a new mechanic will be introduced that will give you the option to use Adrenaline to get you out of the well and get rid of the Custodian from the area for that run so you can freely explore. But Adrenaline is a finite item which there's limited quantity of, and they're also used for other monster deaths, so use them sparsely. However due to adding this new mechanic that also uses Adrenaline, I'll add a few more hidden supplies of it around the game during the next day's patches.

-Some bug fixes here and there.

PLEASE continue sending your thoughts/critiques/requests in the Discussion Board, I'm still working on the game for the next few weeks and want to make the game the best it can be from feedback. So do expect a lot of patches through the next few weeks. Also if you find any bugs/typos/issues, please report them to this thread: http://steamcommunity.com/app/428860/discussions/0/135508833655990580/


---


Now, I will be releasing a few more patches today. Here's what to expect in the next 24 hours: 

-Trafficking Dungeon will be completed. Now many probably haven't arrived at this location yet as it's kind of hidden, but if you've arrived there you've probably noticed a pathway is unfinished. That path will be finished tonight and be fully available hereon out.

-More scenes being added. This will be true for the next few weeks regardless, but adding more and more changes as you do more in the game, lots of hidden triggers, more secrets, etc. This will continue for the next few weeks.

-Fixing any issues people discover in the meantime I can.


ALSO, there is an issue some people on Windows 10 are having. I think I have a solution, but unfortunately Steam doesn't have a good method to send out the update to only Windows 10 users (since it'd delete people's save files and cause some issues on other Windows machines), so I will be making a beta branch in the next few days those on Windows 10 can opt in. Will see if it fixes the issues Window 10 users are having first before fully announcing it, but I think it should help those on Windows 10 having issues with the game.


---


I hope you guys are enjoying the game, and look forward to a lot more updates and content through the next few weeks. Outside of the Lighthouse Upper Floors, the last endings, and the Final Door Area, I'm also adding more and more to the game.

Now then, happy trails to everyone getting lost in the haze~

notes.title: Red Haze Release Notes
notes.notes:
Red Haze is on the eve of its release at the time of writing, and I thought I'd give a breakdown for a few things peeps might like to know about Red Haze on its release. I want to be transparent, so here's just some things I should mention about Red Haze on release date: 


    The game is right now scheduled to release at 8 AM PST / 11 AM EST (did one slight delay for a last second thing), but there's a chance that Valve's store may not open until 9 AM PST / 12 AM EST. If that's so, just know if 8 AM PST comes and goes and the game isn't out, then it'll be hitting a bit past 9 AM PST due to Valve opening shop.

    Red Haze will cost $1.99 USD. It will have a 5% discount for the first week of release. The game will not have another discount until the Summer Sale, in which it will be 5% off again. I like to reward early buyers and be transparent about my sales plans. On that note, don't expect to see Red Haze in a bundle anytime soon.

    Red Haze is not a one and done game. A single ending can be obtained rather quickly if you know what you're doing, but there are a couple dozen endings in the game and as you do more in the game and get more endings, things in the game change. In a single playthrough of Red Haze, you'll only see about 5-15% of the game. 

    Red Haze has 27 endings total, but there will only be 20 endings available on release date. The full details of this are explained in the next bullet point.

    Red Haze will have two major updates that will hit within the first couple weeks of release. The upper floors of the Lighthouse & the Final Door are not available on launch, but these areas wouldn't unlock until about a dozen (or a few dozen) playthroughs anyway. You'll be able to do what you can to unlock the lighthouse upper floors, but it'll be closed off for the time being. The upper floors of the Lighthouse normally don't unlock until you do several different things in the game you have to do across multiple different runs though, if you knew exactly what to do it'd still take several playthroughs, and figuring it out will probably take longer so I hope to patch it in before most players even get to the point of unlocking the upper floors of the Lighthouse. About 5-8 days after release the update will happen, the upper floors of the lighthouse also will net you 6 more of the endings, making the total ending count rise to 26. The 27th and final ending can only be accessed once the other 26 endings have been obtained, and it unlocks the Final Door area, but that also is not in the game at release (given you couldn't even unlock it until the Lighthouse is patched in anyways). The Final Door area will be patched in somewhere between 10-15 days after release.

    Despite the above bulletpoint, I wouldn't hold off from playing. It takes a fair amount of legwork to unlock either of those areas anyway, and they'll be available immediately to those who've unlocked them when patched in. The rest of the game is completed.

    Red Haze has achievements working on PC, but they're not working on Mac at this time. I got them working at one point in development, but it caused SERIOUS stutter issues for Mac testers, so I prioritized playability > achievements. If I figure out a solution to this technical problem, I'll add achievement support for Mac too. But at release achievements only work for PC players.

    The game does have trading cards, and I accidentally had a typo on one of the cards. Sent it a fix which hopefully goes through, but it's looking like it might not. See if you can spot it.

    I've been aided by some wonderfully helpful testers over the last few months on Red Haze, and they've done wonders in helping me squash bugs, typos, and the like. But there's probably still bugs, typos, and the like in the game. I'll try to fix them quickly in the first several weeks of release when more reports are coming in to whatever is reported, to report any bugs/typos/issues, please use this discussion board topic: http://steamcommunity.com/app/428860/discussions/0/135508833655990580/

    I'm a-okay with anyone doing monetized videos on Red Haze. I would appreciate a link to the game's Steam page, but that's not a requirement, just a request.


I learned a lot while working on Red Haze, and I feel like my next project will be much better for it. I hope you guys enjoy Red Haze though, and that it manages to surprise you in some ways.

notes.title: Release Date Feb. 13th Blues
notes.notes:
So game is releasing February 13th. It'll be done before the 13th I think, but I was looking over release schedules and hardly anything else is releasing that day, so it's why I picked it. It wasn't going to make the 6th date like I hoped, I still need to finish up a couple more areas I'm crunching right now and recording dialogue with Rockette's and Starry's VA's tomorrow and the day after.

In the future once my next project, Hollow Bliss is released as well, I'm going to try to avoid specific dates until I'm 100% certain like I am right now. That's one thing I've certainly learnt the hard way, and I do understand if the delays have made some lose interest and I take full responsibility. It can be hard to gauge these things, especially when managing other aspects of your life.

I appreciate the few in beta testing who've been helping me tremendously in polishing the title, they've been helping to make sure this is a fairly smooth launch as far as bugs & typos are concerned and several have been committed to helping there, which I'm grateful for.

I don't want to say too much yet as I do fully believe Red Haze is best experienced going in blind, just knowing the game is not meant for a single playthrough (in fact, to experience everything would take, no joke, at least 27 playthroughs, and probably more due to a few things), and it's been interesting and challenging to design a game with that sort of focus, one where players only experience a small fraction of the game in a single playthrough, and trying to spice up replays so you never fully know what to expect. With a game that demands to be played at least 27 times to get to the true ending, it's challenging making those 27 runs interesting and more different than one might expect.

Still, has been definitely a roller coaster for me developing the game, and I'm sure for some of you following the game with the delays. It will release 6 AM PST / 9 AM EST on the 13th of February (yes, 2017), it will cost $1.99 with a 5% discount off for the first week (so $1.89). It won't go cheaper than that for a while, it will go on sale for 5% again during the next Summer Sale. I like to be transparent about this and not rip off early customers. And I thank all those who've been patient.

notes.title: Red Haze: Finalized Release & Thoughts
notes.notes:
http://store.steampowered.com/app/428860

https://i.gyazo.com/f1a529a5c7229ee65853b71fc89bdc61.png

Red Haze is in active crunch right now, and will be releasing February 6th - 8th. 6th is the goal, 8th is the deadline to allow two days if something comes up last minute. This is finalized, It's basically going to be non-stop work for me, except to break on the 24th & 25th as I'll be playing Resident Evil 7.

Red Haze will be releasing for $1.99 USD, and have a 5% discount on release for the first week, so will be $1.89 for the first week. It won't go on sale for a while after that, until the Summer Sale, which will be discounted the exact same amount, 5% off, $1.89. I also promise it won't be bundled. I like to reward early buyers, its a big policy for me whenever I do releases. I think there is value both to myself and to fans and early adopters to allow a wide window of time before going deeper into discounting. And to be frank, it's not very hard to come by a couple dollars.

Game will also have Steam achievements on Windows PC, cloud saves, & Steam Trading Cards. Unfortunately there will be no achievements on Mac for the time being due to a technical limitation, there is by chance a work around but my efforts thus far have caused issues with the Mac version. Playability over achievements is what I decided.

---

So, some thoughts here before I send the game out as a product. In some ways Red Haze has turned out to be a much better game than I thought it'd be, and in others it hasn't quite lived up to what I wanted it to be. It has been a fantastic learning experience for myself, and I think my future endeavors will benefit from having made Red Haze. I've in earnest learned far more about game design, RPG Maker, myself, spriting, music making, and more during its process I think will help me with future projects.

I don't know how Red Haze will do. I don't think I can know. Before I released Close Your Eyes, for example, I thought people weren't going to like it. I knew all of its flaws, I knew how it could've been better, and I was thinking its purposely cryptic story was going to frustrate people. It turned out doing a lot better than I anticipated, turns out the things I liked about it shined above the flaws for most. Even Take the Dream IX did better than I anticipated, I think it's the shittiest game I've ever made and I finished it out of sheer will to show I could finish it.

So when it comes to Red Haze, it's hard for me to place how people may receive it. I'm expecting some "ow the edge," and some people to find elements of it cringey, and that's fine. The subject matter kind of naturally aligns itself to that, and I don't think all will like my voice acting choices I made for Red Haze. And if I'll be honest, I think the element of Red Haze that most didn't live up to what I wanted it to be was its narrative. There's a story, and in some ways I think I managed to make some interesting story scenes and developments, but it didn't quite come together like I wanted it to in its earlier stages. Characters were cut, scenes were as well, and thus entire plot elements dropped.

On the other hand, I'm anticipating how people receive the game. I sent out some keys to random people who don't know me, I don't know them, and I think it's telling I got the same feedback from everyone: A bit of a slow start, but they slowly get more and more into it and start getting more engrossed in its strange world. Which is good, that was my singular biggest goal with Red Haze, to make a branching game that's not to be experienced in but a single playthrough, but several, with lots of secrets to uncover, endings to obtain, deeper areas to discover, and oddities to figure out. It uses a very unorthodox gameplay design I won't go fully into detail to here, but I think while some things didn't come together how I would've hoped, I think (and hope) it'll be a game that will be very much worth people's $2.

I think it won't be my magnum opus, but I hope you all enjoy it. It's taken a lot longer than I would've liked due to life, motivation, one hell of a year in 2016, working on other things at the same time, breaks, and adding more and taking away at the same time at Red Haze as time has gone on.

I'm kind of expecting some initial negative reviews by people who only experience the tip of the iceberg and never get to see what lurks deeper in the game, and the voice actress for Rockette is worried because she voiced in another RPG Maker Horror game in the past (Uri's Boogie Man, as it were), and has trolls who stalk her and she predicts they'll try trolling the review page for this game when it releases since they resurfaced again for her recently getting word she was voicing in this game. She tried apologizing to me about it, but to be honest I'm not too worried. Even if people not trolling dislike the game, I think there's a lot I can learn from that.

2017 is a big year for me since I either make or break this game making thing for me, but I have a lot of things slated for this year. My plans have changed since my last update on 2017 plans, which I'll try to share in the future. I decided to not go for as strict deadlines, for one, and re-arranged projects a bit more. That'll be for another day, however.

For those helping with testing, there will be a pretty huge update hitting tomorrow, and a second big update hitting at the end of January. I appreciate everyone who's been helping test the game and spotting things I may have otherwise missed.

A late welcome to 2017, and I look forward to seeing y'all play Red Haze. I hope it lives up to your guy's anticipation & expectations, and surprise you in some ways. I will say this though, it by design is a very different game than Close Your Eyes. It was highly experimental for me, and while I learned a lot from it, it's to be seen what y'all think of it. I hope it's enjoyable.

notes.title: 2017 Floor Plan for Yai Gameworks [Goal to Release 8 Games]
notes.notes:
I will keep this post straight to the point, due to some voice actor & personal things I am doing one last & final delay to Red Haze & Hollow Bliss, but this is 100% going to be the last delay (sans some unfortunate incident of some kind). notes.title: A Girl Is Eating From My Garbage, Lonely Yet Not, & Red Haze ; Basic Info & Going Forward Update
notes.notes:
So as some of you guys probably saw, I have delayed Red Haze to 'eventually' release. My actual goal with this is to release the game within the next half a year, before the end of 2016 or during the first few months of 2017, so the delay shouldn't actually be that long. I said before while posting this to the Red Haze page that the delay was because of an idea brewing inside of me I needed to make a reality; whenever I started to work on Red Haze I would work for an hour or two and get some progress done (but much less than my usual 5-12 hour development sessions I'm used to). But I always stopped and didn't fully know why since I still had the urge to create something but my heart was directed elsewhere. A friend helped me realize that what's been stopping me was a selfish creative desire, in Red Haze I kept on getting ideas to add in a big segment based off some thoughts I have had cooped up inside for a couple years, but I decided not to since it was too radically different from Red Haze and didn't really fit with everything else for the game. But it kept on coming back into my head, I tried to push it back to tell myself I could work on it after Red Haze, but in turn it was making me work less on Red Haze as I actually wanted right now to work on that project tossing around in my head and to work on Red Haze between that,

So Red Haze is put on small hiatus, to release 'eventually (though it almost without a doubt will release within the next half a year, I will mention). Red Haze will remain free and I am hoping taking some time to work on a couple other projects will make Red Haze flow more naturally too so I can make it want I want it to be instead of trying to rush elements of it to get it over with. So what am I doing & working on now? 

Firstly, I have started the beginning stages of the bigger medium project which is what had been stirring in my mind and interrupting Red Haze development, Lonely Yet Not. I don't have a lot of details I will share about this quite yet, but it will definitely not release until next year, it is very unorthodox, and has a cast of seven main characters. My artists Rincs has done a fantastic job doing quick concept sketches of them as I work on the early music and designing stages, I'll post a couple minisculed & cut in half rough concept sketches of two of the characters here: 

https://65.media.tumblr.com/b1f8220bdbb8b155329231852cc627db/tumblr_oe6bhmcb2t1se6ntfo1_400.png

We'll talk more about Lonely Yet Not another time.

What I'm really here to talk about is my Halloween project, I actually started with two and decided which one to finish with while the other I'll release at some other point. I originally thought about trying to force Red Haze to be my Halloween project, but since that's not going through, here comes the project I'll be dedicated my development time too as we get early work done on Lonely Yet Not.

A Girl Is Eating My Garbage

That's the name of the game.

It's not a very long project, it's developed as one of my shorter projects. Well, I say that but honestly it'll probably have more development time put into it than both Close Your Eyes and Take the Dream IX had into them. I am undecided if I should put a price on the game or release it freely yet. I hope to put it up on Greenlight next week, as I want to release it on October 28th if possible and if I don't post it on Greenlight soon, there's no way I'll be greenlit in time for that date. Worse comes to shove I'll release it in November, but I'd like to meet that Halloween update, so hoping Greenlight goes swiftly for the title.

A Girl Is Eating My Garbage will be the strangest game I've released yet, it uses a sort of simplistic graphic style so I can do rapid development quickly, and has a lot of unorthodox gameplay elements... For example, you cannot save traditionally. The game starts off with the very thing the game is named off of, a guy is becoming concerned since there is a girl that's eating out of his garbage at night. And not just one night, she keeps on coming back to his garbage to chow down every night. He's getting weirded out and paranoid, and goes out to confront her...

I won't say too much yet as I hope to have the game up on Steam Greenlight in a weeks time, but I hope you guys look forward to it and I am open to answering questions about the title. Most of the information I'll share currently on it will be in response to questions asked of me before it goes up on Greenlight next week.

Thought I'd give you guys an update, and hope you guys look forward to "A Girl Is Eating From My Garbage" going up on Greenlight next week, which hopefully I can get greenlit a bit before Halloween.

notes.title: Final Release Date for Take the Dream IX & Red Haze ; Foreword
notes.notes:
Sorry for all the delays on the store page; Close Your Eyes went through the same sort of thing, for the future I'll remember to make it not display a date when I'm not sure if it'll be releasing on that day specifically.

However, both Take the Dream IX & Red Haze now have official release dates! We'll be releasing Take the Dream IX on March 4th, and follow-up with Red Haze to release on April 1st.

The reason for the delays is the simple answer I've been keeping myself busy (mostly playing games) over the last few weeks, so I haven't been working on them as much as I should of. However, focusing to complete these in the following weeks, and release these two freeware games for you all to enjoy.

In case you're not aware of the other title, currently working on and releasing two games: 

Take the Dream IX: 
http://store.steampowered.com/app/428870/

Red Haze: 
http://store.steampowered.com/app/428860/

Both titles are experimental games, and both were made in a limited time span (while there have been delays, that's more because I've been doing other things than working on the game, honestly). I expect Red Haze to review and be generally better received than Take the Dream IX, but I am also curious how Take the Dream IX will be received, as it's a weird one that gets odder the further in the game you go.

I hope when they release, you guys will give them a shot and leave some feedback; I do ask to give them a fair shake, both of them (but Take the Dream IX especially) don't really give the full experience of the game in the opening moments.

Both of these games may be patched later with additional content based on how they're received, but I'll try to make the updates well-known if they do happen. I hope you all are having some good times, and look forward to letting you all play through these odd little freeware games of mine.
